lessons.title: What agri trade is and how to get ready
lessons.html:
What is agri trade?

Agri trade is the shop side of farming. It is the co-op, the farm store or the input shop in town. Farmers come here to buy seed, fertiliser, animal feed, dip, fencing wire, tools, spares and protective clothing. Some stores also buy grain or sell to the public.

You may work at the counter, in the store room, in the yard where the bags of feed and fertiliser are kept, or at the loading bay. Every job helps the farmer get the right thing at the right time.

Who are the customers?

  • Commercial farmers who buy big orders, often on account.
  • Small-scale and emerging farmers who buy smaller amounts and often pay cash.
  • Farm workers sent by the farmer with an order note.
  • Gardeners and people from town.

Getting ready for work

Before you start a shift, plan your day. A good plan stops mistakes and makes you calm.

  1. Arrive on time and sign in.
  2. Put on your uniform, name badge and safety shoes.
  3. Ask your supervisor what the main jobs are today. Is a truck coming? Is there a special on feed?
  4. Check that your tools are ready: pen, order book, price list, hand trolley, scanner.
  5. Look at your work area. Is it clean? Is anything blocking the walkway?

Know the main product groups

GroupExamples
Crop inputsSeed, fertiliser, lime, crop sprays
Animal health and feedLick, feed, dip, vaccines
HardwareWire, poles, droppers, tools, pipes
Clothing and safetyOveralls, boots, gloves, masks

You do not need to know everything on day one. Ask questions. Learn one shelf at a time. When a farmer asks for something you do not know, say: "Let me find out for you," and ask a senior person. Never guess.

lessons.title: Basic principles of trade
lessons.html:
How the store works

Every store follows the same simple cycle. Goods come in, goods are stored, goods are sold, and money comes in. Then the store orders again.

  1. Ordering: the buyer orders stock from suppliers.
  2. Receiving: the truck arrives. Someone counts the goods and checks them against the delivery note.
  3. Storing: goods are packed on shelves or pallets in the right place.
  4. Selling: the customer chooses goods and pays at the till or on account.
  5. Re-ordering: when stock runs low, the store orders again.

Price, cost and profit

The store pays the supplier a cost price. It sells to the farmer at a selling price. The difference pays wages, electricity, transport and the profit. Example: a bag of lick costs the store R200 and is sold for R250. The R50 is not all profit. Some of it pays for the truck, the staff and the building.

Why stock matters

If the store runs out of maize seed in planting time, the farmer goes to another store and may never come back. If the store buys too much, money is stuck on the shelf and some products expire. That is why counting and recording stock is so important.

The customer is the reason for the job

  • Greet every customer.
  • Listen to what they need.
  • Give the right product and the right amount.
  • Help load heavy bags onto the bakkie safely.
  • Say thank you.

A farmer who is helped well tells other farmers. Word of mouth is very strong in farming areas.

Paperwork you will see

You will see order forms, delivery notes, invoices, till slips and stock cards. Each one is a record. Write clearly, use the right date and sign where you must. If a paper is wrong, tell your supervisor. Do not tear it up or throw it away.

lessons.title: Safety and work ethics
lessons.html:
Safety in the store and yard

An agri store has many dangers. Bags are heavy. Forklifts move in the yard. Some products are poisons. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says the employer must make the workplace safe, and you must also work safely and follow the rules.

Lifting

  • Bend your knees, keep your back straight, hold the load close.
  • Use a trolley or ask for help with heavy bags.
  • Never throw bags down from a high stack.

Chemicals

  • Keep sprays, dips and poisons in their own locked area, away from feed and food.
  • Never open, decant or smell a chemical container.
  • If a container leaks, keep people away and call your supervisor at once.
  • Wash your hands before you eat.

Yard and vehicles

  • Walk in the marked walkways.
  • Keep away from a working forklift unless the driver can see you.
  • Only trained people may drive a forklift.

Fire

Know where the fire extinguishers and exits are. Do not smoke near fertiliser, fuel or chemicals. Report blocked exits.

Work ethics

Work ethics means doing the right thing, even when nobody is watching.

  • Honesty: never take stock or money. Give the correct change.
  • Punctuality: be on time, every day.
  • Respect: treat every customer and co-worker the same, no matter who they are.
  • Reliability: finish what you start. If you cannot, say so.
  • Confidentiality: do not talk about a customer's account or what they buy.

Finishing your shift

  1. Pack away your tools and trolley.
  2. Clean your area.
  3. Hand in order notes and paperwork.
  4. Tell the next person about anything not finished.

Key points

  • Agri trade supplies farmers with the inputs they need.
  • Goods move in a cycle: order, receive, store, sell, re-order.
  • Lift safely and keep chemicals locked away from feed.
  • Be honest, on time and respectful.
  • Ask when you do not know. Never guess.
